title: Faworki angel wings
subtitle: light, crisp Polish fried pastry ribbons dusted with icing sugar
excerpt: Faworki, also known as angel wings or chrust, are thin, egg-rich pastry ribbons deep-fried until golden and crisp, then dusted generously with icing sugar. The dough is made with flour, eggs, sour cream, and a small amount of spirit to prevent the pastry absorbing too much oil during frying. Each ribbon is slashed and twisted before frying so it fans out in the oil.
sourceNotes: Faworki are a traditional Polish sweet pastry eaten at Carnival and Tlusty Czwartek (Fat Thursday), the last Thursday before Lent. Comparable fried pastries exist across Central and Eastern Europe and the Mediterranean: crostoli in Italy, klenater in Scandinavia, and bugie in the Ligurian region of Italy. The name faworki refers to decorative ribbons.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best eaten on the day of frying. Store uncovered at room temperature; a lid traps steam and makes them soft. Will keep for 2 to 3 days but lose crispness.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: fried in oil at 180 degrees C

content.text: Faworki are thin, egg-rich pastry ribbons that are deep-fried rather than baked. The dough is made with flour, eggs, sour cream, and a small measure of vodka or rum; the alcohol evaporates rapidly when the pastry hits the hot oil, which helps the faworki puff and blister rather than absorbing grease. The dough must be rolled very thin, about 2 mm, and each strip is cut with a diagonal slash through which one end is threaded to create the signature twisted ribbon shape.

items.prepNote: for the dough; extra for dusting

content.text: Whisk the egg yolks with the icing sugar until pale and slightly thickened. Add the sour cream, vodka, and melted butter. Mix well.
Add the flour and salt. Mix to a rough dough, then turn out and knead for 5 minutes until smooth and pliable. The dough should not be sticky. Wrap and rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.

Divide the dough into four pieces. Roll each piece on a lightly floured surface as thin as possible, about 2 mm. Cut into strips 3 cm by 12 cm. Cut a 3 cm diagonal slit through the centre of each strip. Thread one end of the strip through the slit and gently pull to create a twisted ribbon.

Heat the oil in a deep-sided saucepan to 180 degrees C. Fry the faworki in batches of 4 to 5, turning once, until golden and puffed, about 1 to 2 minutes per side. The oil must stay at temperature; if it drops below 170 degrees C the pastry absorbs oil rather than frying.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper. Dust generously with icing sugar while still warm. Serve the same day.

attrs.problem: Faworki coming out greasy and heavy rather than crisp and light
attrs.avoid: Avoid frying at too low a temperature; oil below 170 degrees C soaks into the dough before the exterior can seal.
attrs.fix: Use a cooking thermometer and fry in small batches so the oil temperature does not drop when cold dough is added. Allow the oil to return to 180 degrees C between batches.

attrs.problem: Dough tearing when twisted rather than stretching cleanly
attrs.avoid: Avoid working with dough that has not rested or that is too cold.
attrs.fix: Rest the dough for the full 30 minutes at room temperature. If it tears when threading, allow that portion to rest for another 5 minutes before trying again.
